newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition decides not to admit Yadav group.
newsitem.headline: India coalition decides not to admit Yadav group.

text.p: India's United Front coalition has decided not to admit into its fold the breakaway group of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party headed by a scandal-tainted leader, the front's spokesman said on Friday.

Laloo Prasad Yadav resigned as Bihar chief minister earlier on Friday after a court in the state capital Patna issued a warrant for his arrest in a corruption case in which he has been indicted by the federal police.

His arrest was later stayed by the Supreme Court until an appeal from the leader was heard. Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group, which was formed earlier this month following differences within Gujral's party, named Yadav's wife Rabri Devi as the new Bihar chief minister.
"The decision is not to give membership to the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)," Information Minister Jaipal Reddy told reporters after a meeting of senior leaders of the coalition in the Indian capital.

"The decision on the continuation of the three ministers has been left to the discretion of the prime minister," Reddy said of the ministers in Gujral's cabinet whose status had become uncertain following the formation of the breakaway RJD.

Yadav had earlier refused to resign over the scandal, involving alleged embezzlement of animal welfare funds in which he says he is innocent. Gujral's coalition had been divided on whether to admit the RJD, fearing it could hurt the alliance's image.
